dimensions.title: Monitoring (local and remote metric monitors)
dimensions.researchSummary: Object-path prefix `subsystem:MonitoringManager` and the two lookup calls `findLocalMonitor(name)` / `findRemoteMonitor(nodeName, monitorName)` are doc-verified in both the LiveUpdate page and the Designer API guide "Monitoring Machine Health" (real URL: https://developer.disguise.one/api/guides/monitoring ; the guessed /monitoring-machine-health 404s). Every monitor is a `MetricMonitor` (d3.pyi:25989) whose only value accessors are `seriesAverage(title, nSamples) -> float` and `seriesAverageByIndex(idx, nSamples) -> float`; nSamples=1 is documented as "the latest value in the series", and the guide recommends a 10-sample rolling average for alerting. Documented (monitor name -> series title) pairs: "fps"->"Actual" (LiveUpdate doc + guide), "GPUProfiler"->"Total" (+ "Video Upload","Capture Upload","Compositor","GUI","Render Everything","DMX" from disguise-one's official Grafana dashboard), "CPU"->"Total", "GPUMemory"->"Usage(MB)", "ProcessMemory"->"Usage (MB)" (guide), "Machine"->"CPU Time","GPU Time","CPU Memory","GPU Memory","Disk" (Grafana dashboard, unit percent), "Disk"->"Read (MB/s)","Write (MB/s)" (Grafana dashboard; guide says Disk over LiveUpdate is still "in development (DSOF-20732)"). Remote node names are "<hostname>:d3" ("Replace MACHINE_NAME with the hostname of the target machine"). Discovery expressions (`object.remoteNodes()`, `[m.name for m in object.localMonitors().all()]`, `[s.name for s in object.graphDescriptor(False).dataSeries]`) exist in the stub but their LiveUpdate use is only inferred; `FifoDataSeries.samples()/capacity()` (raw buffer, min/max) are new in r34.0. Nothing in this dimension is sensibly writable from a Stream Deck (setters exist only for monitor config such as pollInterval/name). Recommended updateFrequencyMs: 500 for live readouts (fps, GPU/CPU ms), 1000 for rolling averages and the "Machine" percentages, 2000-5000 for memory, 10000+ for discovery lists; never 0 for monitors (per-frame pushes at 60 Hz). Embedded Python is 2.7 (use `False`, not `false`; dict/list comprehensions are fine).
dimensions.verifySummary: Verified all 28 candidates against freshly downloaded sources (guide, Live Update page dump, help.disguise.one graphs and RenderStream-graphs pages, r33.1/r34.0 change logs, Python environment page, disguise-one grafana-liveupdate dashboard JSON) and the local r34.0 d3.pyi. Every cited d3.pyi line number resolved to the exact member and signature quoted, and every document excerpt was found verbatim (guide at https://developer.disguise.one/api/guides/monitoring; the /monitoring-machine-health URL 404s as reported). 27 of 28 candidates are supported. The one rejection-level item is mon-renderstream-prefetcher-names: the 'renderstream'/'prefetcher' constants live on _BlipValue classes that are not MetricMonitors, and two of the series labels the researcher quoted ('network latency (ms)', 'engine latency (ms)') do not exist on the help page - marked unsupported/unverified. Confidence corrections: several direct members on documented object paths (remoteNodes, seriesAverageByIndex, monitor meta properties, RemoteMonitor.nodeName, Machine.nodeName, Subsystem.isEnabled, searchString) were upgraded from inferred to doc-verified under the brief's rule (pyi member exists AND object-path prefix documented); multi-hop chains through MonitorCollection (_BlipValue) or graphDescriptor() snapshots were held at inferred because no doc shows such intermediates traversed in a LiveUpdate expression. Writability corrections: RemoteMonitor.nodeName and MonitoringManager.searchString have pyi setters (writable yes, but do not ship set presets); GraphDescriptor fields all have setters but act on a per-call snapshot (keep unknown). Unit finding for the lead: the help page defines the CPU graph's 'Total Time (ms)' as working time + present-wait time in milliseconds, so the guide's 'CPU utilisation' heading is misleading - label the CPU Total readout in ms pending a live check. The 'Machine' monitor (percent series) and 'Disk' MB/s series come only from the official Grafana dashboard, not developer docs, and 'Machine' is absent from the help page's Local graph list - keep needs-live-test. Missed items of real operator value: Machine.hasIncomingHouseSyncSignal()/incomingHouseSyncSignal()/allRequiredOutputsGenlocked() give a genlock indicator over the doc-verified Machine:\"<name>\" path, filling the gap the researcher reported for the health endpoint's Genlock category. Sources saved under verify_monitoring/ (guide.txt, helpgraphs.txt, rsgraphs.txt, r340.txt, r331.txt, env.txt, grafana.json, pymm.txt, pymgr.txt, accessres.txt).

candidates.description: Local machine FPS, latest sample ("per head" FPS graph, the number shown in the FPS bug bottom-right of the track). Canonical LiveUpdate monitoring example.
candidates.range: 0..project refresh rate (e.g. 60). Guide alert rule: warning 5-9 fps below expected, error >=10 below.
candidates.updateRationale: Value changes every frame (60 Hz). 500 ms gives a readable 2 Hz readout on a button; the guide's own examples use 100 ms for a dashboard but that is 10 variable updates/s per button in Companion.
candidates.source: https://developer.disguise.one/api/session/liveupdate (local dump liveupdate.txt, 'Examples: subscribing to graphs') and https://developer.disguise.one/api/guides/monitoring ('Subscribe to local FPS')
candidates.sourceQuote: object: "subsystem:MonitoringManager.findLocalMonitor(\"fps\")", properties: ["object.seriesAverage(\"Actual\", 1)"] ... By using a value of 1, we end up obtaining the latest value in the series.
candidates.verifierNote: Re-opened liveupdate.txt:516-517 and guide.txt ('Subscribe to local FPS'): exact object/property strings present, including the sentence 'By using a value of 1, we end up obtaining the latest value in the series.' d3.pyi:26068 `def seriesAverage(self, title: str, nSamples: int) -> float:` on MetricMonitor (Resource). Grafana live-dashboard.json:183-187 uses it verbatim. No setter anywhere; read-only.
candidates.notes: pyi: d3.pyi:26068 `def seriesAverage(self, title: str, nSamples: int) -> float:`. Also used verbatim by the official Grafana dashboard (grafana-liveupdate/provisioning/dashboards/live-dashboard.json:183-187, panel 'FPS').

candidates.description: Local FPS averaged over the last 10 samples - the smoothing the guide recommends for alert/feedback colouring so content loads do not trip false positives.
candidates.range: Guide: 'Warning: average FPS drops by 5-9 fps below expected framerate; Error: average FPS drops by 10 fps or more below expected framerate'
candidates.updateRationale: Already smoothed; 1 s is enough for a colour-state feedback and halves traffic versus the raw readout.
candidates.sourceQuote: The second argument to seriesAverage is the number of samples to average. Using a value of 1 returns the latest value in the series. For alerting, a rolling average over 10 data points is recommended to avoid false positives during transient events like content loading
candidates.verifierNote: guide.txt 'Interpreting FPS values' contains the quoted sentences verbatim (10-point rolling average, warning 5-9 fps, error >=10 fps). The literal call seriesAverage("Actual", 10) is not printed in any doc; it is the doc's stated recommendation applied to the doc-verified signature (d3.pyi:26068). Acceptable as doc-verified; behaviour when nSamples exceeds FifoDataSeries.capacity() (d3.pyi:17316) is undocumented as the researcher says.
candidates.notes: Semantics: average of the newest nSamples entries in the series FIFO. Behaviour when nSamples exceeds the buffer (FifoDataSeries.capacity(), r34+) is not documented.

candidates.description: Local FPS averaged over 60 samples (about one second at 60 fps) - the 'Average FPS' series in disguise's official Grafana dashboard.
candidates.updateRationale: One-second window, so updating faster than 1 Hz adds nothing.
candidates.sourceQuote: "name": "Average FPS", "path": "object.seriesAverage(\"Actual\", 60)"
candidates.verifierNote: raw.githubusercontent.com/disguise-one/grafana-liveupdate/main/provisioning/dashboards/live-dashboard.json lines 190-191: "name": "Average FPS", "path": "object.seriesAverage(\"Actual\", 60)" under objectPath line 183 findLocalMonitor("fps"). Source is disguise-one's official repo, not developer.disguise.one; flag that distinction in the preset notes.

candidates.sourceQuote: def samples(self) -> List[float]: ":return Snapshot of the FIFO contents in order; applies SAMPLE_DELTA mode if set." ... r34.0 change log: 'FifoDataSeries.samples / def samples(self) -> List[float]: ... FifoDataSeries.capacity'

candidates.verifierNote: d3.pyi:17322 `def samples(self) -> List[float]:` with docstring ':return Snapshot of the FIFO contents in order; applies SAMPLE_DELTA mode if set.' and 17316 capacity() with ':return FIFO buffer size; samples() returns at most this many.' r340.txt:242-246 lists FifoDataSeries.samples and FifoDataSeries.capacity as r34.0 additions - so r34.0.3 has them, r33.x does not. Oldest-first ordering is not stated explicitly ('in order'), as flagged.

https://developer.disguise.one/python-api/useful-strings contains no monitoring snippets (only an OscDevice path named 'PluginMonitor'); the per-release Python API change logs mention monitoring only for r33.1 (MonitorCollection.all/active/expired return type -> List[MetricMonitor]) and r34.0 (FifoDataSeries.samples/capacity added). The RenderStream tab graphs (Renderer / Profiling / Stream / Render skew / Response skew / Texture parameter latency) have no documented findLocalMonitor names; the pyi constants 'renderstream' and 'prefetcher' are on _BlipValue classes and may not be monitor names at all. Health-status states exposed by REST (/api/session/status/health: averageFPS, videoDroppedFrames, videoMissedFrames, states[{name,detail,category,severity}] with severity ok/warning/error/busy/offline and categories Connection/Output/Genlock/Devices) have no documented LiveUpdate equivalent; the guide explicitly says System API endpoints 'cannot be polled via the Live Update API' and discourages REST polling. dimensions.title: Transport / track playback state
dimensions.researchSummary: CONCLUSION: transport state IS reachable from a LiveUpdate object expression, and the exact documented syntax is the one the module HELP already uses: object path `transportManager:default`, property paths under `object.player.*` (TrackPlayer), `object.track.*` (current Track), `object.timecode.*` (TimecodeTransport) and the TransportManager's own fields. Evidence: (1) Disguise's official plugin guide https://developer.disguise.one/plugins/getting-started/ subscribes exactly `autoSubscribe('transportManager:default', ['object.player.tRender'])` through the LiveUpdate Vue composable; (2) the Designer expression guide https://help.disguise.one/designer/configuration/expressions/accessing-resources uses `transportmanager:default.timecode` (lower-case type; both casings appear in official docs, the LiveUpdate-context one is camelCase); (3) the OSC monitoring guide documents `transport.player.playMode.__str__()`, `transport.brightness`, `transport.volume`, `transport.statusString`, `transport.tcStatusString`, `transport.beatToTimecode(currentBeat).__str__()`, `track.description`, `track.trigger_note`, `track.bpmAt(currentBeat)`, `track.noteAtBeat(track.sectionToBeat(currentSection))` where `transport` is 'The Transport Manager' and `track` is 'The current track within the transport' - in LiveUpdate `object` plays the role of `transport` and `object.track` the role of `track`; (4) d3.pyi r34.0 confirms every member and setter. The transports Python guide does NOT expose `d3.transportManager` or `TransportManager.default`; in Python the manager is reached via `guisystem.currentTransportManager` (GuiSystem is a Subsystem, so `subsystem:GuiSystem` + `object.player.tRender` is a plausible but untested alternative that would follow whichever transport is current). Key facts for preset design: `object.player.playMode.state` is the LIVE play state enum (Play=0, PlaySection=1, LoopSection=2, Stop=3, HoldSection=4, HoldEnd=5 per TrackPlayer constants) whereas `object.play_mode` is only the timecode-chase CONFIG with a different numbering (0 Play, 1 Play To End Of Section, 2 Loop Section) - do not confuse them. `object.brightness`, `object.volume`, `object.engaged` have setters (LiveUpdate-settable), but whether a LiveUpdate `set` on them behaves like a TransportCommand is undocumented. `object.player.speed` is new in r34.0. Playhead values (`tRender`/`tCurrent`) are in beats (== seconds at the default 60 bpm); use `object.track.beatToTime(...)` for guaranteed seconds and `object.beatToTimecode(...).__str__()` for a TC string. Designer eval is Python 2.7 (developer.disguise.one/python-api/environment: 'Designer uses Python 2.7 for its embedded interpreter'), so avoid f-strings; `__str__()`/`str()` and comprehensions are fine. REST /api/session/transport is command-oriented (all POSTs: play, stop, playsection, playloopsection, gotoframe/time/timecode/track/section/tag/note/next/prev, returntostart, brightness, volume, engaged) and its GET state endpoints (activetransport, transports, tracks, setlists, annotations) expose uid/name/engaged/volume/brightness/playmode(string)/currentTrack/receivingTimecode/setList - all of which except `receivingTimecode` map cleanly onto LiveUpdate properties listed below.
dimensions.verifySummary: All 49 candidates survive verification; none are rejected. Every cited d3.pyi line number resolves to the claimed member with the claimed signature and setter state (checked 51302-51660 TransportManager, 48303-48370 SuperTransportManager, 50155-50252 TrackPlayer, 33884-33990 PlayHead/PlayMode, 47975-48302 SuperTrack, 49568-50138 Track, 48985-49052 Timecode, 49172-49291 TimecodeTransport*, 43113 SetList, 40424 Resource, 19201+ GuiSystem), and all 11 cited web pages returned 200 and contain the quoted text (plugins/getting-started line 421 has the verbatim `autoSubscribe('transportManager:default', ['object.player.tRender'])`; the OSC monitoring-custom page lines 1504-1745 contain every transport./track. expression the researcher quoted; accessing-resources line 1562 has `transportmanager:default.timecode`). Confidence corrections: tr-34 (`object.timecode.current.__str__()`) and tr-42 (`object.description`) are upgraded to doc-verified because the OSC guide lists those exact expressions; tr-12 (`isFreeRunning`) is downgraded to inferred because the member has no docstring and the researcher's semantics are a name-based guess. The r34.0 change log confirms TrackPlayer.speed under Added > Class.properties, and its Removed/Modified sections contain no transport entries. The researcher's open questions stand (tRender vs tCurrent, type-prefix casing - note python-api/guides/resources line 165 says paths are 'always lowercase' while the LiveUpdate examples use camelCase, LiveUpdate set semantics on brightness/volume/engaged, PlayMode.__str__ literal strings). One open question can be closed from the stub: Track.findBeatOfNextSection (d3.pyi:49757) is documented to return the track length when no further section exists, giving a safe replacement for the sectionToBeat(i+1) pattern in tr-26/tr-28. Notable skipped members are listed in missed, chiefly monitorString (documented in the OSC guide), findBeatOfNext*/Last* feature helpers (also documented there), sendTransportCommands, on_clock_lost/regained, smpteClockType(), and sectionInfo().

object.track.findBeatOfNextSection(object.player.tRender) (Track, d3.pyi:49757, ':return The beat of the next section, or the length of the track if no more sections are found') - documented end-of-track fallback that resolves the open question about sectionToBeat(i+1) past the last section; use for next-section name and section-remaining countdown instead of tr-26/tr-28's index arithmetic.

object.track.findBeatOfNextNote / findBeatOfLastNote / findBeatOfNextTag / findBeatOfLastTag(object.player.tRender) (Track, d3.pyi:49747/49717/49767/49737) - all four are shown in the OSC guide (oscmon.txt lines 1760-1775) as the way to build 'feature' variables; findBeatOfNextNote returns DBL_MAX when none, so guard in Companion.
object.track.formatNoteForBeat(beat, object.player.tRender) (Track, d3.pyi:49787) - returns the note with a '.<n>' suffix for sections ahead; convenient for a 'next cue' label.

object.track.sectionInfo(i).tStart / .tEnd (Track.sectionInfo d3.pyi:49911; SectionInfo d3.pyi:42797, tStart/tEnd documented) - documented to return 'the end of the track if no such section exists', another safe way to get section bounds.
object.track.sectionLengthBeats(i) (Track, d3.pyi:49922) - section duration for progress bars.
object.track.tc_adjust (Track, d3.pyi:49600, setter 49608) - per-track timecode adjust; useful config readout next to the TC lock indicator.

object.track.lengthInSec (SuperTrack, d3.pyi:48072, read-only) and object.track.bpm (48025, setter 48028) - only mentioned in passing; lengthInSec is the guaranteed-seconds denominator for a progress bar.

object.player.playHead.playJustTriggered (TrackPlayer.playHead d3.pyi:50198 -> TrackPlayHead(PlayHead); PlayHead.playJustTriggered d3.pyi:33902) - a one-frame 'play just started' pulse; marginal but could drive a Companion trigger.
object.player.sectionTestMode (TrackPlayer, d3.pyi:50217, bool, no docstring) - skipped state flag.

object.on_clock_lost / object.on_clock_regained (TransportManager, d3.pyi:51383/51397, Options {0:'Keep Playing',1:'Stop'} / {0:'Reset to start',1:'Play from current'}) - timecode config readouts with documented enum meanings.

object.sendTransportCommands / sendTransportCommandsMode (TransportManager, d3.pyi:51485/51495, 'Whether transport commands should be sent or blocked (stops actors getting updates)') - an important operational safety state for a director in a session.
object.trackToLoad (TransportManager, d3.pyi:51591, str, setter) - startup track name.
object.smpteClockType() (TransportManager method, d3.pyi:51649) - transport-type-agnostic frame-rate enum with documented fallback to the project clock type; better than tr-36 for a generic preset.
object.startupBrightness / object.startupVolume (SuperTransportManager, d3.pyi:48337/48347, setters) - config values behind tr-15/16.
object.timecode.current.t (Timecode.t, d3.pyi:49000) and object.timecode.current.fps() (49037) - raw float and fps of the incoming timecode.

object.timecode.adjust__sec_ (TimecodeTransportClocked d3.pyi:49235 / TimecodeTransportBeat 49204, setter) and object.timecode.updateStatusString (TimecodeTransportLtc, d3.pyi:49288) - LTC-specific status/offset readouts.
object.timecode.transportManager (TimecodeTransport, d3.pyi:49190) - back-reference, useful only for sanity checks.
object.descriptionExtended (Resource, d3.pyi:40445, 'A more detailed description of the Resource, including its status') - may give a richer one-line transport status string than description.
subsystem:GuiSystem / object.currentSetList (GuiSystem, d3.pyi:19235, setter 19241) - companion to tr-48 if that path resolves.
openQuestions: tRender vs tCurrent: both are undocumented in the stub (PlayHead d3.pyi:33922/33926). Disguise's plugin guide uses object.player.tRender; the Python track guide uses guisystem.player.tCurrent for 'current playhead position (in beats)'. Which one the timeline readout follows (and whether tRender lags by a frame) needs a live check before choosing the preset default.

Units: the LiveUpdate doc states all times are beats (track time); the plugin guide prints tRender with an 's' suffix. Beats == seconds only at the default 60 bpm. Presets should either document this or use object.track.beatToTime(object.player.tRender) (tr-03).

Type-prefix casing: developer.disguise.one/plugins/getting-started uses `transportManager:default`, help.disguise.one accessing-resources uses `transportmanager:default`, the Python resources guide says paths are always lowercase, yet the LiveUpdate doc uses `Machine:"<name>"`. Both casings appear in official docs; which the r34.0.3 parser accepts (or whether it is case-insensitive) is unverified. The module HELP uses the camelCase form.

'default' is the documented name of the default transport manager (help accessing-resources). Projects with renamed or multiple transport managers need transportManager:"<name>" (tr-49) or getByUID(); no doc shows these with the transportManager type specifically. REST GET /api/session/transport/transports lists names/uids to plug in.

Writing via LiveUpdate `set` on object.brightness / object.volume / object.engaged: setters exist in the stub and the LiveUpdate doc says set commands are undoable and persistent, but nothing documents whether such a set is equivalent to TransportCommand.makeBrightness/makeVolume (propagated to actors as a transport command). REST POST /api/session/transport/{brightness,volume,engaged} is the documented command path. Needs a live test before shipping set presets.

JSON shape of object.player.playMode when subscribed directly (PlayMode is a _BlipValue structure with a `state` int) is untested; presets should subscribe to `.state` or `.__str__()`. The literal strings returned by PlayMode.__str__ are not documented anywhere I found.

Transports Python guide says `timecode_transport.timecode` for 'the current timecode receiver', but the r34.0 stub exposes TimecodeTransport.current (d3.pyi:49182) and no `.timecode` member. I used `.current`; the guide may be stale or `.timecode` may be a dynamic attribute.

REST GET activetransport exposes a boolean `receivingTimecode`; no pyi member with that meaning was found on TransportManager/TrackPlayer/TimecodeTransport. Closest are statusString / tcStatusString (strings), preRollMatch and player.isFreeRunning - a boolean 'TC LOCK' feedback would need string matching or a live check of isFreeRunning semantics.

The OSC monitoring guide's `Timecode(seconds)` function variable and the currentBeat/currentTime/currentSection/currentFeature* variables are OSC-Event-Transport-local. The LiveUpdate doc says only `object` is bound (plus `from d3 import *`), so I assumed they are NOT available in LiveUpdate property paths and rewrote them with Track methods.

Behaviour of object.track.sectionToBeat(i + 1) past the last section is undocumented (sectionCueToBeat returns -1 for non-sections; sectionInfo returns 'the end of the track if no such section exists'); the next-section-name preset (tr-26) may return '' or error at the final section.
subsystem:GuiSystem (tr-48) is inferred from the documented `subsystem:` prefix and GuiSystem(Subsystem) in the stub; untested, and GuiSystem is described as GUI-local.

MultiTransportManager (d3.pyi:27722, transportManagers list) has no documented Designer-expression object path; REST GET transports lists multitransports. Unknown whether `multiTransportManager:<name>` resolves.

D3State.lockedToDirector (d3.pyi:10597) would be a useful 'locked to director' indicator, but the D3State singleton (`state` in Python) has no documented Designer-expression object path, so no candidate was proposed.
https://developer.disguise.one/python-api/useful-strings contains no transport-state snippets (only guisystem.track.addNewLayer and guisystem.track.splitSectionAtBeat), so nothing from it was used.

https://developer.disguise.one/api/session/status and /sequencing were grepped and contain no transport-state fields; the r34.0 change log lists only TrackPlayer.speed, EventTransportOSC.speed and EventTransportMidiNote.transportSpeed* as transport-related additions (Removed/Modified sections had no transport entries in my grep).
Python 2.7 caveats for property paths: no f-strings; `__str__()` and `str()` fine; integer arithmetic on section indices fine; float division fine because tRender/beatToTime are floats.

dimensions.title: Track / Section / Layer inspection and keyframe read/write
dimensions.researchSummary: Evidence base: the Live Update page (liveupdate.txt) verbatim documents track:track_1 with object.lengthInBeats / object.layers / object.getLeafLayers(VariableVideoModule), chained layer timing object.layer.tStart/tEnd/tLength, and the keyframe chain object 'track:track_1.getLeafLayers()[0]' with property 'object.findSequence("pos.x").sequence.key(0).v' (writable via set) plus the all-keys comprehension using .key(i).localT and .nKeys. The Python Track & Sequencing guide confirms layer.name (layers use name, not description), layer.tStart/tEnd/tLength in track beats, layer.enabled, layer.findSequence("brightness"), keyseq.nKeys()/key(i)/t(i), key(i).v = value, key(i).r = resource, and that keyframe times are Track beats, not layer-local. d3.pyi (r34.0) supplies the full member/setter list: SuperTrack (lengthInBeats w, lengthInSec ro, bpm w, layers, nLayers(), findLayerByName(name)->Layer, getLeafLayers(type), beatToTime/timeToBeat/bpmAt), Track (cues: TimeSequence[Cue] with n()/getT(i)/getV(i); nSections(), sectionInfo(i).tStart/tEnd, sectionToBeat, sectionLengthBeats, beatToSection(beat), noteAtBeat, cueAtBeat, tagAtBeat(beat,type)/tagsAtBeat, layerByName(name), trigger_note w, tc_adjust w), SuperLayer (name w, enabled w, enabledIncludingParents ro, render/renderEnable w, tStart w, tEnd ro, tLength w, anchored ro [new r34.0], crashed ro, isDormant ro, track, container), Layer (fields, findSequence, nSequences(), keyTimes(), moduleType), FieldSequence (name, userName, typeName, disableSequencing w, isPatched, expression, sequence, getSequencedValue(t)), KeySequence (key(i), nKeys(), t(i), keys, looping w, evalString(t)), Key (localT w, interpolation w), KeyFloat.v w, KeyString.s w, KeyResource.r w, Cue (note w, section w, getTags()), Tag (text, type; CUE=1, TC=0, MIDI=2), SectionInfo (iSection, tStart, tEnd). Units: every track/layer/key time is in beats; seconds come from lengthInSec, beatToTime(beat) or timeToBeat(sec); the guide warns beats-to-seconds is 'not always a fixed relationship' (bpmAt varies). Layer-by-name: no 'layer:' prefix is documented anywhere and the guide says layers are unnamed Resources; the documented routes are index-based 'track:track_1.getLeafLayers()[0]' or, per pyi, 'track:track_1.findLayerByName("Name")' / 'track:track_1.layerByName("Name")' chained in the object path (same chaining style as the documented getLeafLayers()[0] and MonitoringManager.findLocalMonitor("fps")), or a comprehension over object.layers filtering on l.name. Python is 2.7 (environment page), so no f-strings; dict/list comprehensions are fine. Best Stream Deck candidates: layer enabled toggle, layer brightness/pos/scale/text first-keyframe knobs, layer extents readout, track length/bpm, section list with notes and CUE tags, tc_adjust knob.
dimensions.verifySummary: Re-verified all 57 candidates against d3.pyi (SuperTrack 47975-48327, Track 49568-50039, SuperLayer 47795-47941, Layer 21752-21881, Key/KeySequence 21123-21296, FieldSequence 17103-17278, Cue 9872, Tag 48428, SectionInfo 42797, TrackTransitionInfo 50254, TimeSequence 647, Resource 40424, VariableVideoModule 53250-53582) and against freshly downloaded copies of the LiveUpdate page (local dump), the track-and-sequencing guide, expressions guide, useful-strings, python-api/docs, environment, docs/track and the r33.1/r33.2/r34.0 change logs (all HTTP 200, stripped into verify_track_layer/). Every cited member exists with the stated spelling, arity and setter status, and every quoted excerpt appears in its source; 56 of 57 candidates are supported at the researcher's confidence. The one rejection for shipping is mod-live-clip-values (module: prefix is only evidenced as expression syntax; stays unverified). Corrections: Key interpolation constants are at 21130-21132 (not 21131-21133); setNoteAtBeat is at 49942; Cue is a Resource (not _BlipValue) so cue-table chaining relies on the documented resource-reference resolution; SuperLayer.container has a setter (47815) although track does not; Resource.description on an unnamed layer will likely yield the class name rather than an empty string. Confirmed real doc/stub conflicts the lead must test live: getLeafLayers() no-arg on Track (pyi requires a type), nKeys without parentheses in the LiveUpdate comprehension, guide's layer.sequences / track.tags / layer.moduleType() not matching pyi, and sectionLengthBeats taking a cue index rather than a section index. Python 2.7 confirmed on both environment and docs pages.

openQuestions: getLeafLayers() arity: the LiveUpdate page uses 'track:track_1.getLeafLayers()[0]' with no argument, but d3.pyi:48147 declares SuperTrack.getLeafLayers(self, type: Type) (required) while only SuperLayer.getLeafLayers() (d3.pyi:47929) is no-arg. Needs a live test; fallback is object.layers[0] or getLeafLayers(VariableVideoModule)[0].
nKeys with or without parentheses: the LiveUpdate comprehension uses '.sequence.nKeys' (no call) but d3.pyi:21265 and the Python guide use nKeys(). Test both; pyi form is the safer default.

No 'layer:' object-path prefix is documented anywhere fetched (liveupdate, expressions guide, paths, locator). The track guide says 'Layers are unnamed Resources', so type:name lookup probably does not apply. Layer-by-name therefore relies on track:<t>.findLayerByName("..") / track:<t>.layerByName("..") (pyi-only members) or a comprehension over object.layers. Behaviour on missing/duplicate names is undocumented (None -> expression failure per expressions guide).

The 'module:<layer name>' prefix is documented only as expression syntax (expressions guide: module:video.frameNumberDisplay); whether Designer expressions used as LiveUpdate object paths accept it is unverified, and the guide advises not accessing Module objects directly.

Name quoting for tracks with spaces: liveupdate.txt shows track:track_1 (underscore) and Machine:"<machine name>" (quoted); the expressions guide documents both forms for projector:. Assume track:"Track 1" works but it is not shown verbatim.

JSON serialisation of TimeSequence[Cue] (object.cues), Type (object.moduleType), ReflectionValue (getSequencedValue().value) and Expression (findSequence().expression) is not covered by the documented serialisation table; the explicit comprehensions above avoid these.

Guide/stub mismatches: the track guide mentions track.tags and layer.sequences; neither exists in the r34.0 pyi (Resource.tags is List[ResourceTag], a different concept; Layer exposes fields / sequence(i) / nSequences()). Also guide writes layer.moduleType() but pyi declares a property.

Which properties actually accept 'set': only KeyFloat.v is documented. enabled, name, tStart, tLength, localT, interpolation, looping, disableSequencing, KeyString.s, KeyResource.r, bpm, lengthInBeats, tc_adjust, trigger_note all have pyi setters; the doc states 'There is no way to know if setting a property will work before trying it.' Anchored layers reject extent changes.
render vs renderEnable (d3.pyi:47868/47875) have no docstrings; semantics and relation to the Layer editor unknown.

Units: LiveUpdate page says lengthInBeats is 'in beats (seconds)', the Python guide says the beat/second relationship 'is not always a fixed relationship' (bpmAt varies per beat). Preset labels should say 'beats' and offer lengthInSec / beatToTime for seconds. tc_adjust units are not stated.

Section index vs cue index: sectionLengthBeats docstring says its parameter is 'the cue index of the section' whereas sectionInfo/sectionToBeat/beatToSection use a 0-based section index; verify on a track with non-section cues (tags/notes only).

Field decorated names beyond 'pos.x', 'pos.y', 'scale' (LiveUpdate doc) and 'brightness', 'opacity', 'text', 'red', 'green', 'blue' (expressions guide) are undocumented; enumerate with [f.name for f in object.fields] on the target project.

Current-section / current-layer presets need the playhead beat (TrackPlayer.tCurrent d3.pyi:50234, TrackPlayer.activeLayers d3.pyi:50171, TrackPlayer.track d3.pyi:50250) which belongs to the transport dimension; confirm that dimension supplies a documented object path for the TrackPlayer so beatToSection(...) can be fed.

Python 2.7 caveats for propertyPath strings (environment page): no f-strings, integer division is floor for ints, print is a statement; list/dict comprehensions are fine. Avoid calling mutating methods (setFloat, setExpression, setNoteAtBeat, insert, remove) inside a propertyPath since it is re-evaluated on every update.

dimensions.title: Stage / Screen objects
dimensions.researchSummary: Screens in Designer r34 are Resource > Object > Display subclasses: Screen2 (UI name "Surface" = projection surface), LedScreen, Projector, DmxScreen (via DmxDisplay > DownloadableDisplay), plus the Stage container (Object). LiveUpdate object paths use Designer expression syntax `type:name`, where `type` is the class name (the LiveUpdate doc uses `screen2:screen_1`; help docs use `projector:"projector 1"`, `videoclip:"sample/george.jpg"`, `module:video`, `transportmanager:default`; the LiveUpdate doc uses `Machine:"<machine name>"`). Names with spaces/special chars are either double-quoted (`projector:"projector 1"`, newer versions) or sanitised to underscores (`projector:projector_1`, all versions; only a-z A-Z 0-9 _ allowed). Any resource can also be reached by `getByUID(0x...)` (documented as a LiveUpdate object path). Only `screen2:` and `projector:` prefixes are documented; `ledscreen:` and `dmxscreen:` follow the same rule but are inferred, and no `stage:` prefix is documented at all. Geometry: Object.offset/rotation/scale are writable Vec values serialised as `{x,y,z}`; the LiveUpdate doc explicitly shows `screen2:screen_1` / `object.offset -> { x: 0.0, y: 3.0, z: 0.0 }` and that a partial set `{x: 4.0}` preserves the other fields. Operator-relevant writables common to every screen type (Display base): master_fade (0..1 output brightness, not shown in visualiser), holdOutput (freeze output), blendMode/alpha/content (visualiser compositing), renderLayer (On/Off stage/Frontplate/Backplate...), resolution. Type-specific: Screen2.projectorViewBlending/screenBackground; LedScreen.luminanceNits/viewingAngle (visualiser only); Projector.render_mode, simulatedShutterOpen, autoSoftEdge, feather, lumens, barnDoor*; DmxScreen.status__ (Mute/Active = DMX output kill), universe, iChannel, luminance. Valuable read-only state: description, isBad/isInError, isReceivingFromTrackingSource, hasTrackingSource, mesh.description, isConnected, Projector.hasFeedAssigned()/isActiveOutputModeNone, DmxScreen.isTableMalformed(), Stage.nDisplays(). Expression property paths are Python 2.7 eval'd with `from d3 import *`; list/dict comprehensions allow one-button multi-field readouts.
dimensions.verifySummary: All 55 candidates survive verification: every cited d3.pyi member exists with the stated spelling, arity, type and setter status, and every quoted doc excerpt was found verbatim in freshly re-downloaded pages (help.disguise.one accessing-resources/functions/output-properties/appearance-properties, developer.disguise.one liveupdate/stage guide/expressions guide/useful-strings/r34 change log). Confidence corrections: stage-038, 042, 043, 045 (Projector.simulatedShutterOpen, hasFeedAssigned(), isActiveOutputModeNone, fieldOfView) qualify as doc-verified under the rubric because the members exist and the `projector:` prefix is documented, though their semantics remain unevidenced. Minor line-number fixes: Object render-layer constants are at 29161-29166; Projector.renderMode(value) is at 35844; getSupportedOutputModeNames at 35856. Confirmed the researcher's central caveat: the strings `ledscreen:`, `dmxscreen:` and `stage:` appear in none of the 12 fetched pages (grep count 0), so all LedScreen/DmxScreen/Stage candidates correctly stay inferred; getByUID(...) is the documented fallback path. Two doc inconsistencies worth flagging to the lead: the Python stage guide uses `dmx_screen.channel = 101` and `fixture_type = 0`, but the r34 pyi has property `iChannel` (channel is a method channel(iArray)) and `fixtureType` (r34 change log confirms fixture_type was removed); and resolution is set with Int2 in the stage guide but Vec in useful-strings while the pyi types it Vec2. No page fetched states the embedded Python version, so the Python 2.7 syntax constraint is taken from the task brief, not verified here.

candidates.description: User-visible name of a projection Surface (class Screen2). Sanity-check that the object path resolved; good as a button label.
candidates.updateRationale: Names change only on rename; poll slowly.
candidates.sourceQuote: screen2:screen_1 | object.description | "screen 1" - the user-visible name of the object.
candidates.verifierNote: Verified. liveupdate.txt lines 160-165 show the exact pair `screen2:screen_1` / `object.description`. Resource.description at d3.pyi:40437-40442 has no setter.
candidates.notes: Resource.description has no setter (d3.pyi:40438). Rename via object.path (writable, d3.pyi:40520) is NOT recommended from a Stream Deck.

candidates.description: Position of the surface in metres relative to parent. Serialised as JSON {x,y,z}. Writable; partial JSON set ({x:4.0}) preserves y/z.
candidates.updateRationale: Static screens change rarely, but if a tracking source drives the object it updates every frame; 250 ms keeps a readable readout without flooding Companion.
candidates.sourceQuote: If a property value is a JSON object (e.g. screen2:screen_1 / object.offset -> { x: 0.0, y: 3.0, z: 0.0 }) it is possible to only set one field of the property. e.g. {x: 4.0}
candidates.verifierNote: Verified. liveupdate.txt lines 235-239 show `screen2:screen_1 / object.offset -> { x: 0.0, y: 3.0, z: 0.0 }` and partial set `{x: 4.0}`. Object.offset property + setter at d3.pyi:29223-29233, type Vec.
candidates.notes: Use setToDisguiseJSON with {"x":<n>} for a single-axis nudge. Docstring: 'Position in the scene, in meters; relative to parent object in hierarchy, and mesh position. UserName: Offset'. Set commands are undoable and persist on the Director.

candidates.description: Scalar X position readout (metres). Reading is documented via expression syntax (projector:projector_1.offset.x); writing a bare float to this sub-path via LiveUpdate set is not documented.
candidates.sourceQuote: Further specify the x, y or z coordinates by using the . operator again e.g. projector:projector_1.offset.x
candidates.verifierNote: Read path verified: accessing-resources.txt line 1549 `projector:projector_1.offset.x` and expressions-guide line 237. Vec.x has a setter at d3.pyi:53672-53673, but no doc shows a LiveUpdate `set` on a scalar sub-path; writable stays unknown. The `screen2:` prefix is documented in liveupdate.txt.
candidates.notes: For writing, prefer subscribing to object.offset and sending partial JSON {x: n} (documented). Whether set on object.offset.x works is an open question.

candidates.description: Euler rotation in degrees (x,y,z) relative to parent; writable Vec.
candidates.updateRationale: Tracking-driven objects update per frame; static ones rarely.
candidates.sourceQuote: Rotation around x, y, z axes, in degrees; relative to parent object in hierarchy, and mesh orientation. UserName: Rotation
candidates.verifierNote: Verified. Object.rotation + setter at d3.pyi:29264-29274, docstring quote exact. stage-guide.txt line 211 `my_obj.rotation = Vec(0.0, 90.0, 0.0)`.
candidates.notes: Stage guide example: my_obj.rotation = Vec(0.0, 90.0, 0.0). Partial JSON set applies per LiveUpdate doc rule for JSON-object values.

candidates.description: Scale factor applied to mesh vertices (for the default 1x1 m Rectangle mesh this is the physical size in metres). Writable Vec.
candidates.sourceQuote: Controls the size; this is a scale factor applied to mesh vertices  UserName: Scale
candidates.verifierNote: Verified. Display.scale + setter at d3.pyi:12203-12213 with quote 'Controls the size; this is a scale factor applied to mesh vertices'; Object.scale at 29276-29284 says only 'The scale of the object.' stage-guide.txt line 125 has the Rectangle 1m x 1m sentence.
candidates.notes: Stage guide: 'Default is an internally generated mesh called Rectangle which has a 1m x 1m dimension, meaning the scale parameter can be used to define absolute sizes'. Display overrides Object.scale with identical semantics.

candidates.description: One-subscription geometry readout (dictionary values are serialised recursively). Read-only as a dict; write via the individual properties.
candidates.updateRationale: Composite readout; half-second is plenty for a display button.
candidates.sourceQuote: Dictionaries: A Python dictionary is returned as a JSON object, where the values in the dictionary are serialised according to this table. This allows for more complex queries in a single property subscription.
candidates.verifierNote: Verified. liveupdate.txt line 266 (Dictionaries) and lines 298/323 show dict literals inside property expressions. All three members exist on Object/Display.
candidates.notes: Python 2.7 dict literal syntax is fine.

candidates.description: Per-screen output brightness (0..1) applied at the Feed output level; not reflected in the visualiser. The most operator-relevant writable knob on any screen.
candidates.updateRationale: Operator toggles it live and wants immediate button feedback; value changes are sparse so 250 ms is cheap.
candidates.sourceQuote: Controls output brightness; is not reflected in the visualiser  Category: Output  UserName: Master fade
candidates.verifierNote: Verified. Display.master_fade + setter at d3.pyi:12085-12096, docstring exact. output-properties.txt 'Master fade' section: 'It ranges from 0 to 1. Use this to reduce the brightness of a physical screen to compensate for cameras'.
candidates.notes: Help: 'It ranges from 0 to 1. Use this to reduce the brightness of a physical screen to compensate for cameras'. Preset ideas: Fade 0 / 0.5 / 1 buttons with setToDisguiseNumber. Property is on Display, so it exists on Screen2, LedScreen, Projector and DmxScreen alike.

candidates.description: Freeze this screen's output (per-screen Hold) while sequencing continues.

candidates.verifierNote: Verified. Object.renderLayer + setter at d3.pyi:29242-29262, Options {0..7} exact. openQuestions: Prefixes `ledscreen:` and `dmxscreen:` are not shown in any fetched document (only `screen2:`, `projector:`, `videoclip:`, `module:`, `transportmanager:`, `Machine:`, `track:`, `subsystem:`, `domain:` appear). They follow the documented type:name rule with the class name, but must be confirmed on a live Director - easiest by Alt+dragging from the LED/DMX screen editor into an expression field (Designer writes the canonical reference) or by sending a subscribe and reading the error reply.

No `stage:` prefix is documented. Stage-level properties (autoSoftEdge, displays, nDisplays) are only reachable if the Stage editor offers 'Copy UID' for getByUID(), or via some other undocumented root. Needs a live check.
Prefix case sensitivity: the LiveUpdate doc uses `Machine:"..."` (capital M) while help docs use lowercase `projector:`. Unknown whether `Screen2:` / `LedScreen:` are also accepted.

Quoted-name syntax (`projector:"projector 1"`) is described as unavailable 'in older versions of Designer'; no version number is given. r34.0.3 should support it, but the sanitised form (`projector_1`) is the safe fallback. The Companion module must pass the double quotes through inside the JSON object string (the LiveUpdate doc shows `Machine:"<machine name>"` as an object path).

Setting a scalar sub-field path directly (propertyPath `object.offset.x` with a number value) is undocumented; the documented method is subscribing to `object.offset` and sending partial JSON `{x: 4.0}`. Test which works before building single-axis nudge presets.
JSON shapes for Vec2 (resolution, {x,y} assumed), Mat (world/local), Colour and ColourShift are not documented; only Vec ({x,y,z}) and Resource ({uid,path,type}) are.
Display.alpha: pyi types it float and help text says full = 255; actual numeric range (0-1 vs 0-255) unverified.

Projector.simulatedShutterOpen, outputBrightness, hasFeedAssigned(), isActiveOutputModeNone, fieldOfView have no docstrings - whether shutter/outputBrightness affect real feed output or only the visualiser is unknown.
Object.externalUpdate is writable but the effect of setting it false while a tracking source is attached is not documented.
Whether LiveUpdate `set` is refused on a locked resource (Resource.locked) is not documented; the doc only says 'There is no way to know if setting a property will work before trying it'.

The help site states resource field names 'cannot be definitely relied upon to continue to use the same name over versions'; r34.0 already renamed DmxScreen.fixture_type -> fixtureType. Presets should carry a version note (targets r34.0.3).
The raw GitHub markdown sources linked from help.disguise.one (github.com/disguise-one/help.disguise.one/...) returned 404 via raw.githubusercontent.com; the rendered HTML pages were used instead.

dimensions.title: Expression Variables and operator knobs
dimensions.researchSummary: Storage model (d3.pyi r34.0): ExpressionVariablesDevice(Device) has one writable property `container` (ExpressionVariablesContainer), whose `variables` is a writable `List[ExpressionVariable]`. Each ExpressionVariable is a _BlipValue (not a Resource) with writable `name` (str), `type` (int enum 0=Float, 1=String, 2=Function), `defaultFloat` (float), `defaultString` (str), `errorText` (str), plus `makeExpression() -> str`. There is no separate "value" field: the official "Set ExpressionVariable to a value" snippet on python-api/useful-strings writes `var.defaultFloat`, so for device variables defaultFloat/defaultString ARE the live value. Timeline (layer) variables live on ExpressionVariablesModule.fields -> List[ConnectedField] (each has `.variable` and `.value: ReflectionValue`, plus setFloat/setString). Object-path prefix: no page shows an ExpressionVariablesDevice referenced by expression; the documented convention is `<class>:<name>` (track:, screen2:, projector:, module:, transportmanager:default, Machine:"name", and for a Device subclass `mididevice:bcf2000`), so `expressionvariablesdevice:<device name>` is INFERRED, with `getByUID(0x...)` as the doc-verified rename-proof fallback. Proposed paths: read one float `object.container.variables[<i>].defaultFloat` (index) or `[v.defaultFloat for v in object.container.variables if v.name == "<var>"][0]` (by name); read all `{v.name: (v.defaultFloat if v.type == 0 else v.defaultString) for v in object.container.variables}`; set one by subscribing to the index path and sending set (pyi setter exists; LiveUpdate documents set through an equivalent nested chain `.sequence.key(0).v`, so inferred). Designer's embedded interpreter is Python 2.7 (dict/list comprehensions OK, no f-strings). No change-log entries for ExpressionVariable* between r30.8 and r34.0. Other doc-verified knobs found: transportmanager:default / object.brightness (master brightness), screen2:<name> / object.master_fade and object.offset, module:<layer> / object.brightness, track:<t>.getLeafLayers()[i] / object.enabled and object.findSequence("brightness").sequence.key(0).v.
dimensions.verifySummary: All 23 candidates re-verified against d3.pyi (r34.0) and freshly downloaded pages under verify_exprvars/; every cited member exists with the stated spelling, arity and setter status, and every quoted excerpt was found verbatim (liveupdate.txt, useful-strings.txt:162-172, help-ext-proto.txt:1605-1612 mididevice example, help-access-res.txt:1500-1563, help-variables.txt:1533-1545, help-ev-device.txt:1458-1493, expressions.txt:210/522/545, environment.txt:132 Python 2.7). dimensions.title: RenderStream cluster health
dimensions.researchSummary: Designer's LiveUpdate docs (liveupdate.txt and the Monitoring guide) explicitly document four RenderStream expressions on object path "subsystem:RenderStreamSystem": getWorkloadReceiveStatuses(<workloadId>), getStreamReceiveStatuses(<workloadId>, <machineName>), getWorkloadInstances(<workloadId>) and getWorkloadInstance(<workloadId>, <instanceIndex>).health(); plus hasTakenOverFailedMachine() on a Machine. d3.pyi (r34.0) confirms the signatures: workload is a Python int, instanceIdx is int, machineName is str. getWorkloadInstances returns List[WorkloadInstance] whose fields are machineName:str, status:int, isProcessRunning, isStopping, isDroppingFrames, isDroppingInputFrames, isHighActiveLatencyDetected, isremoteTextureEmpty, unrecoverableError (all bool); health() returns WorkloadHealth {message:str, details:str, status:int, priority:int}. Receive statuses are List[SubscribedStreamStatus] with receiver (Machine resource -> {uid,path,type}), streamIdentifier {streamHandle,streamName,workloadId}, subscriptionWanted, subscribeSuccessful, activeLatency, recentReceived/recentSent/recentDuration, totalReceived, totalDroppedPackets, tLastReceived/tLastDropped/tLastError, tLastErrorMessage, and methods recentReceivedFPS(), recentSentFPS(), generateStreamStatusMsg(bool). None of the int status/priority fields carry Options docstrings, so enum meanings are unknown. The REST /api/session/renderstream page provides workload discovery (GET layers -> GET layerstatus returns workload.uid plus per-instance machineName/state/healthMessage/healthDetails), and the LiveUpdate doc also points to the deprecated V1 /api/v1/renderstream/workloads and the 'Copy UID' menu on the Cluster Workload widget. Two pyi-only (inferred) discovery paths avoid REST entirely: RenderStreamSystem.getWorkloadLayers() -> map[int, Layer], and a RenderStream layer's object.moduleConfig.workloadId (Layer.moduleConfig -> RenderStreamModuleConfigBase.workloadId:int). The layer route also exposes cluster-level health (moduleConfig.cluster.workloadHealth, anyInstanceIsRunning, nInstances, instanceHealth(i), instanceMachine(i).statusString/isOnline). Display-friendly comprehensions (joined strings, counts, any()/all()/min()/max()) are Python 2.7-safe but marked inferred. Suggested throttles: 1000 ms for instance/health state (matches the doc's configuration example), 1000 ms for receive-rate counters which otherwise change every frame, 2000-5000 ms for discovery values. No RenderStream API changes are listed in the r34.0 Python API change log; textureParamStatus()/StreamStatus/lastChangeTime were added in r33.1.
dimensions.verifySummary: Re-opened every cited source: liveupdate.txt (full RenderStream section lines 532-609 and object-path/serialisation sections 134-275), d3.pyi classes RenderStreamSystem 40327, WorkloadHealth 57674, WorkloadInstance 57725, SubscribedStreamStatus 47620, StreamIdentifier 47018, StreamStatus* 47132-47200, Subsystem 47736, RenderStreamClusterBase 39826, RenderStreamMachine 39965, RenderStreamModuleConfig(Base) 40189/40237, RenderStreamModuleBase 40113, ClusterPool 8455, RenderStreamAsset 39614, StreamObject 47045, ActiveWorkload 1048, TextureParamStatusManager 48911, Machine 23762, Layer.moduleConfig 21821, SuperTrack.getLeafLayers 48147; and downloaded (all HTTP 200) /api/guides/monitoring, /api/session/renderstream, /python-api/api-changes plus r34.0/r33.2/r33.1/r33.0 change logs, /api/v1-notice, /api/paths and /specs/session.swagger.json into verify_renderstream/. Result: 40 of 41 candidates are supported - every method/property name, spelling and argument list exists exactly as stated, the subsystem:RenderStreamSystem, Machine:"name" and getByUID prefixes are documented, and the four core expressions plus hasTakenOverFailedMachine() appear verbatim in both the Live Update page and the Monitoring guide. Corrections: (1) roughly half of the d3.pyi line numbers are off by 1-8 lines (e.g. 47706 is tLastReceived not totalDroppedPackets, 47692 is tLastError not tLastErrorMessage, 58045 is 'optional' not 'map', 47183 is StreamStatusManager not RenderStreamSystem.streamStatus) - corrected numbers are in each note; (2) direct member chains on the documented subsystem path meet the doc-verified rule and were upgraded from inferred; comprehension composites stay inferred; (3) rs-any-instance-error's note is wrong: any([]) is False, so a stopped workload reads as healthy; (4) rs-metric-monitor is rejected as unverified - RenderStreamMetricMonitor is a _BlipValue, not a MetricMonitor, and no doc names a series; (5) the layer route (track:...getLeafLayers(RenderStreamModule)[n]) remains inferred because docs only show a no-argument getLeafLayers() inside the object expression while pyi SuperTrack has only the typed overload; (6) framerateFraction pyi Options include 1/4 but the swagger layerconfig says divisor values 1,2,3 only. No RenderStream changes in the r34.0 change log; textureParamStatus, StreamStatus and lastChangeTime were added in r33.1 as the researcher stated. Missed high-value members: RenderStreamModuleBase.mode/sceneName/animationSpeed (writable layer knobs), activeWorkload(id).instanceStreams(i) -> StreamObject.isStreamOnline, cluster controller/controllerActive(), and RenderStreamMachine.loadFactor/streams.

The developer site has no page for /api/v1/renderstream/workloads (V1 is deprecated per /api/v1-notice; docs only exist in-app at http://[serverip]/docs/v1). Whether comprehension-based subscriptions that call .health() inside a list push updates when health changes; the doc explicitly says health is computed and should be subscribed per instance.

Behaviour when the workload is stopped or the instance index is out of range: does getWorkloadInstances return [] and getWorkloadInstance raise (producing an {error} message)? Companion module handling of {error} replies for a feedback should be checked.
Whether large uint64 workload IDs / stream handles are emitted as JSON numbers (precision loss above 2^53 in Companion's JSON.parse) or as strings.

No documented object-path prefix for RenderStreamMachine or ClusterPool resources (only Machine:"name", track:, screen2:, subsystem:, domain:, getByUID()). The layer route (track:<t>.getLeafLayers(RenderStreamModule)[n].moduleConfig...) is the only pyi-backed way found to reach cluster/pool objects.

Control actions: RenderStreamModuleConfig.startWorkload()/stopWorkload()/reconfigureWorkload() and RenderStreamClusterBase.stopWorkload() exist in the pyi, but LiveUpdate evaluates property paths on subscribe, so putting them in a propertyPath would fire on subscription; the documented control path is REST POST /api/session/renderstream/startlayers|stoplayers|restartlayers|synclayers|failover|failoverpool, which the Companion LiveUpdate module cannot call.
Units of SubscribedStreamStatus.activeLatency and RenderStreamSystem.activeLatency() (frames vs seconds) are undocumented.

Python-version note: Designer's LiveUpdate expressions are Python 2.7; all proposed comprehensions avoid f-strings and use %-formatting, but the api-changes pages do not state the embedded Python version, so this remains an assumption from the task brief.

dimensions.title: Failover / d3Net / machine and session state
dimensions.researchSummary: Evidence base: d3.pyi r34.0.256372 (D3NetManager 10166-10340, D3NetManagerSystem 10341-10359, Machine 23762-24458, MachineStatus 24609, State 46975, SessionSystem 43090-43110, ReleaseVersion 39182, D3State 10395-10786, Resource 40424, netsys_NetworkAdaptor 57875), the LiveUpdate doc, the D3Net Python guide, the Status/Failover/System REST pages, the Monitoring guide, the Python Environment page, the Python reference index (Global Variables) and per-class reference pages. Doc-verified object prefixes for this dimension are Machine:"<name>" and getByUID(<uid>) (both shown with object.hasTakenOverFailedMachine() in the LiveUpdate doc) plus subsystem:<SubsystemClass> (shown only for MonitoringManager and RenderStreamSystem, both class X(Subsystem) in the pyi). Machine exposes everything an operator wants per named machine: hasTakenOverFailedMachine(), failed, failoverDisabled, networkConnected, active, role, runningAs, targets, hostname, IP_address, name, machineType/typeName, isGuiVisible. For 'the local machine / the director without knowing its name' there is no documented LiveUpdate object path; two inferred routes exist: (1) subsystem:D3NetManagerSystem with object.d3NetManager.localMachine / .director / .machines (D3NetManagerSystem(Subsystem) has a read-only d3NetManager property, pyi 10350, reference page confirms), and (2) the module global d3NetManager (pyi:46, listed under 'Global Variables' in the Python reference index; the LiveUpdate doc says property paths run with 'from d3 import *' and d3.pyi has no __all__), used directly inside the property path. Session class itself is empty in the pyi; session name lives on SessionSystem(Subsystem).sessionName. Designer version is only reachable via ReleaseVersion static methods (versionString(), major()/minor()/micro(), versionName()); project name via state.projectName (D3State, read-only). Writable knobs in this dimension are limited and mostly dangerous (director/understudies/role/hostname setters); the only sensible set targets are d3NetManager.timeout (automatic failover timeout, float, 0 = disabled) and d3NetManager.normal_preset (str). Machine health sub-states (Connection/Output/Genlock/Devices with severity Ready/Warning/Error/Busy/Offline) are reachable via d3NetManager.machineStatus(nodeId).states. Version notes: Machine.getNetworkAdaptors and netsys_NetworkAdaptor link speeds were added in r33.1 (D3NetManager.directorIsX1/machineIsX1 removed then, X0 variants remain); Machine.bandwidthSources/hasHDMICapture added in r34.0; D3State.track/player/currentTransportManager removed in r30.8.
dimensions.verifySummary: All 43 candidates are supported; no rejections. Every cited d3.pyi member exists with the stated spelling, arity and setter status (checked D3NetManager 10166-10340, D3NetManagerSystem 10341-10359, Machine 23762-24458, MachineStatus 24609, State 46975, SessionSystem 43094-43110, ReleaseVersion 39182-39309, D3State 10395-10786, Resource 40424, netsys_NetworkAdaptor 57875), and every doc quote was found in the re-downloaded pages under verify_failover/ (LiveUpdate, d3net guide, failover/status REST, monitoring guide, environment, docs index Global Variables, machine/d3netmanager/d3netmanagersystem/sessionsystem/releaseversion/d3state reference pages, expressions guide, r33.1 and r34.0 change logs). Confidence levels as assigned are correct: fo-01..fo-20 are doc-verified because the Machine:\"name\" / getByUID() prefixes appear verbatim in the LiveUpdate doc and the members are in the pyi with matching Read-Only flags on the reference pages; fo-21..fo-43 stay inferred because subsystem:D3NetManagerSystem, subsystem:SessionSystem, the module globals d3NetManager/state and bare type names as '<any resolvable object>' paths are not shown anywhere for LiveUpdate (the doc only demonstrates subsystem:MonitoringManager and subsystem:RenderStreamSystem and says 'all Designer types are available', not globals). Minor corrections: SessionSystem class is at d3.pyi:43094 (sessionName 43103), Resource.isBad/isInError are at 40459/40483, targets setter is at 24146-24147, hasDedicatedGui is at 24022. fo-08's role enum mapping and fo-09's runningAs semantics remain inferred (no docstrings; 'MachineRole' type used by machineRoleToString has no class in the pyi). The r33.1 change log confirms getNetworkAdaptors/netsys link speeds under Added and directorIsX1/machineIsX1 under Removed. Notable skipped members are the per-machine genlock/PTP/VFC health calls on Machine (allRequiredOutputsGenlocked, syncStatus, vfcPTPLockState, vfcTemperature, vfcSysAlertMissing*), Machine.httpPort/localApiEndpoint for REST URL building, MachineStatus.tUpdated, and SessionDiscoverySystem.getSessionAPIEndpoint.

openQuestions: subsystem:<ClassName> resolution: the LiveUpdate doc only shows subsystem:MonitoringManager and subsystem:RenderStreamSystem. D3NetManagerSystem and SessionSystem are Subsystem subclasses in the pyi (10341, 43090) but whether the lookup key is the class name for every subsystem must be tested live. If it fails, fall back to using the globals (d3NetManager / state) inside the property path with any working object, or discover the D3NetManager uid via fo-35 and use getByUID().

Global names in the LiveUpdate eval namespace: the doc says 'all Designer types are available (via from d3 import *)'. d3.pyi has no __all__ and declares module-level d3NetManager, state, paths, resourceManager (lines 40-49), and the Python reference index lists them under 'Global Variables', so a plain import * should expose them - but the LiveUpdate context may be narrower than the /python/execute context. One NameError test settles it.

What 'localMachine' means for a Companion connection to a non-Director: the LiveUpdate doc says subscribe messages are 'sent to the Director', and the Working-with-Sessions guide says to target the Director's hostname. If Companion points at an Actor/Understudy it is unknown whether expressions evaluate on that machine (localMachine = that Actor) or are forwarded. Recommend the module config note: connect to the Director; use d3NetManager.director/actors/understudies for the rest.

Machine.role enum: no Options docstring on role (d3.pyi:24123); mapping Solo=0, DedicatedDirector=1, NonDedicatedDirector=2, Actor=3, Understudy=4, MobileEditor=5, UnknownRole=6 is inferred from Machine class constants (d3.pyi:23771-23887). Verify with a live read on a Director and an Actor.
Machine.networkStatus (int) enum is undocumented; Machine.active vs networkConnected semantics undocumented.

Machine.runningAs: assumed to be the failed Actor an Understudy is impersonating (mirrors REST health 'runningAsMachine'); confirm, and check what it returns when not taken over (self? null resource?).

Discrepancy: D3Net guide writes d3net.directorMode = True and d3net.understudy = True, but the r34.0 pyi and the D3NetManager reference page mark directorMode/understudy read-only (no setter). Treated as read-only.

Is there a Designer-expression prefix for the D3NetManager resource itself? D3NetManager.__username__ = 'd3net' (d3.pyi:10173) and Resource paths are 'objects/[class]/[name].apx', so something like d3net:<name> may resolve - no doc shows it and the resource name is unknown; do not ship without a test.

Failover COMMANDS are not reachable through LiveUpdate set: D3State.cmdMachineFailed(hostname)/cmdMachineRestored(hostname) (d3.pyi:10749/10752) are methods, and a propertyPath calling them would execute on every evaluation - a hazard, never put them in a subscription. The correct control surface is REST POST /api/session/failover/failovermachine and /restoremachine (body {machine:{uid,name}}) and /applydefaultrouting; the Companion module would need an HTTP action for these.

Update semantics for computed expressions (method calls like hasTakenOverFailedMachine(), comprehensions): the doc only defines updateFrequencyMs as a maximum rate. The RenderStream section notes computed 'health()' must be subscribed individually, suggesting computed values are re-evaluated per cycle rather than change-driven; if so, the suggested frequencies above are also the evaluation cost. Verify with changeTimestamp behaviour.
Machine.getNetworkAdaptors() on a remote Machine resource: unknown whether it returns that machine's adaptors, the local ones, or an empty list.
Machine.nodeId is optional[int]: machineStatus(None) / getIsNodeInSession(None) will raise inside the expression; comprehensions must filter 'if m.nodeId is not None'.
state.isInShow, state.lockedToDirector and state.enableBlackout have no docstrings; semantics inferred from names only.

Exact string formats of ReleaseVersion.versionString() vs versionName() vs asString() are unknown; subscribe once and pick. There is no per-remote-machine version member in the pyi - remote versions are only in REST GET /api/service/system/detectsystems.
The 'currentPreset' field of GET /api/session/failover/settings has no obvious pyi counterpart (grep found none); only normal_preset exists on D3NetManager.
Python 2.7 reminder for property paths: dict/list comprehensions and conditional expressions are fine; no f-strings; integer division truncates; None comparisons use 'is not None'.

# Dimension report: Designer expression (object path) syntax and Python 2.7 caveats

Target: Designer r34.0.3 / d3.pyi `__version__ = 'r34.0.256372'` (d3.pyi:22). All quotes below are verbatim from a page fetched in this task or from the local stub.

## (a) Grammar of a resource reference

### `type:name` form
- help.disguise.one accessing-resources: "The simplest and most readable method for building a reference to a known Resource in the system is to use the type:name syntax to refer to a Resource." and "to reference a Projector, the expression projector:"projector 1" is used to refer to the Projector itself. To reference a video clip which originates from a file in a subfolder, videoclip:"sample/george.jpg" can be used."
  https://help.disguise.one/designer/configuration/expressions/accessing-resources.html
- developer.disguise.one guides/expressions: "By Name: Use the type:name syntax. For example, projector:"projector 1" refers to a projector named "projector 1". If the name contains spaces or special characters, it's best to enclose it in quotes. If not, you can replace spaces and special characters with an underscore (_), like projector:projector_1."
  https://developer.disguise.one/python-api/guides/expressions

### Names with spaces / special characters
- Quoted form is the current recommendation (above). Sanitised form: "In older versions of Designer, the quoted name syntax is not available. It is instead possible to reference names using a "sanitised" identifier. The name of "projector 1" referenced in the expression above would be sanitised to projector_1. Names in expressions are unable to contain spaces, dashes and other characters, which are valid for names in Designer. Any character which is not a letter in the alphabet, a number or an underscore must be replaced by an underscore (_). In older versions, this is not available for / characters." (accessing-resources)
- Layer-expressions page: "Names can only contain the characters a-z A-Z 0-9 _." and "This can cause conflicts when two Resources share the same name after normalisation" https://help.disguise.one/designer/configuration/expressions/layer-expressions
- The sanitised name is not the user-visible name: "projector:projector_1.description - this produces a text result which contains the real name of the Resource (without the _ character decoration.) i.e. "projector 1"." (accessing-resources)
- LiveUpdate doc uses both styles in the same document: `track:track_1`, `screen2:screen_1` and `Machine:\"<machine name>\"` (liveupdate.txt, raw HTML confirmed `Machine:` capital M and `track:` lowercase).

Recommendation for presets: use the quoted form for anything typed by an operator (`track:"Track 1"`), since Companion variables can contain spaces; document the underscore fallback.

### Type prefix = lowercase Python class name (not `__username__`)
- LiveUpdate doc uses `screen2:screen_1` while d3.pyi:41825-41832 shows `class Screen2(Display)` with `__username__ = 'Surface'`. So the prefix is the internal class name, not the UI name.
- Resources guide (paths use the same rule): "The type in the path is always the internal type (i.e. never __username__) and always lowercase. A safe method to get the type part of a path for a known object is to use the type() function - type(my_obj).__name__.lower()." and Resource.path docstring d3.pyi:40513-40516: "Paths to internal resources are generally of the form `objects/[class]/[name].apx`, e.g. `objects/camera/cam1.apx`." https://developer.disguise.one/python-api/guides/resources
- Documented prefix examples: `projector:`, `videoclip:`, `transportmanager:default` (accessing-resources); `ledscreen:screen`, `camera:cam_1` (https://help.disguise.one/designer/configuration/expressions/examples/camera-angle-example); `track:`, `screen2:`, `Machine:` (LiveUpdate).
- Layers are the exception: they are referenced through `module:<layername>` — "module:NameOfModule.brightness*0.5 ... You cannot have any spaces in the layer name" (https://help.disguise.one/designer/configuration/expressions/linking-layers), `module:video.frameNumberDisplay` (layer-expressions), `module:this.brightness` (variables page). Caveat for LiveUpdate: "layer references are only valid for the period of time that the layer is active on the timeline" (layer-expressions). Prefer `track:x.getLeafLayers()[i]` or `getByUID(...)` for layers.

### Case sensitivity
- Identifiers/fields/functions are case-sensitive: "Expressions are case-sensitive, so a variables or functions called hello are distinct from another called HELLO" (https://help.disguise.one/designer/configuration/expressions/expressions-overview); "Expressions are no longer case-insensitive - variables, fields and functions are looked up in a case-sensitive manner" (r27.10 note, https://help.disguise.one/designer/configuration/expressions/backward-compatibility).
- Case of the type prefix itself is NOT documented. The LiveUpdate doc's `Machine:` vs `track:` suggests the prefix is case-insensitive, but no source states it. Use lowercase (matches every help-site example and the path rule "always lowercase"). Open question.

### `subsystem:`, `domain:`, `getByUID(...)`
- `subsystem:<PythonClassName>`: only documented in the LiveUpdate page: `subsystem:MonitoringManager.findLocalMonitor("fps")`, `subsystem:RenderStreamSystem`. Class name keeps its capitalisation there. d3.pyi:47736 `class Subsystem(_BlipValue)`, d3.pyi:27218 `class MonitoringManager(Subsystem)`, d3.pyi:40327 `class RenderStreamSystem(Subsystem)`.
- `domain:<name without "Domain" suffix>`: LiveUpdate uses `domain:MappedMedia` while the class is d3.pyi:24793 `class MappedMediaDomain(Domain)`. d3.pyi:14635 `class Domain(_BlipValue)`; DomainManager has `getDomainByType(self, type: Type) -> Domain` (d3.pyi ~14650).
- `getByUID(<uid>)`: functions page: "For example: getByUID(0x123456789012345).description returns the name of the Resource the user right-clicked on." https://help.disguise.one/designer/configuration/expressions/functions ; accessing-resources: "Right-click on the titlebar of the editor window ... Click "Copy UID" ... getByUID(0x123875234) - this is an immutable reference to the Resource". LiveUpdate: `object: "getByUID(<machine UID>)"`. Note `getByUID` is an expression-language function; it does not exist in d3.pyi (grep returned nothing) and not in the Python reference page, so it is only usable in the object part, not in the Python property part. LiveUpdate serialises uids as `"0x0123456789abcdef"` hex strings, so a uid read from one subscription can be pasted directly into `getByUID(0x...)`.

### None-guarding in the object part
- "Attempting to access properties when there is no object will fail and the expression will not evaluate ... It is possible to test if an object is valid by using an if, for example if(transportmanager:default.timecode, "has timecode", "no timecode") but there is no method to conditionally access fields" (accessing-resources). So None-guards belong in the Python property part (see (d)).

## (b) Chained calls in the object part
- LiveUpdate: `object: "track:track_1.getLeafLayers()[0]"` and `object: "subsystem:MonitoringManager.findLocalMonitor(\"fps\")"`; "Objects are referenced using Designer expression syntax."
- backward-compatibility page: "It is now possible to call functions on Resources within expressions. This is an advanced feature ... For example you can use the expression track:track_1.sectionToBeat(1) to return the time in beats for the second section on track 1. These functions are not documented due to the internal and potential for change in future."
- Index operator incl. negative indexes: "array[-1] would select the last item in the array" https://help.disguise.one/designer/configuration/expressions/operators
- Only Designer-expression syntax is available in the object part (functions like `if(cond,a,b)`, `and/or/not`, `[]`, `.` access, method calls). Python comprehensions/conditional expressions are only documented for the property part. Strings: "Arithmetic operators such as + cannot be used to combine strings" (operators page). d3.pyi note: SuperTrack.getLeafLayers is declared with a type argument (d3.pyi:48147 `def getLeafLayers(self, type: Type) -> List[Layer]`), the no-arg form is only on SuperLayer (d3.pyi:47929); the LiveUpdate doc nevertheless calls `track:track_1.getLeafLayers()` with no argument.

## (c) List of valid type prefixes
No official list exists on any fetched page. Evidence-backed set:
- Documented: `track`, `screen2`, `projector`, `videoclip`, `ledscreen`, `camera`, `transportmanager`, `Machine`/`machine`, `module` (layers), `subsystem`, `domain`, `getByUID(...)`; external protocols (not resources): `osc:`, `dmx:`, `dmx16:`, `midi:` (guides/expressions), `valid_osc:` (variables page).
- Inferred rule: any `Resource` subclass lowercased (path rule above). d3.pyi Subsystem subclasses (for `subsystem:`): AlertNotificationSystem ArtNetSystem AudioSystem BlueFishSystem CITPSubsystem CalibratorSystem CameraCalibrationSystem CameraVideoInSystem CommsSystem D3NetManagerSystem DeltaSystem DisplayManagerSubsystem Dmx DomainManager GuiSystem HTTPSockpuppetSystem HoldOutputSystem IPVideoInSystem IndirectionSystem LogicalVideoInSystem LumaKeyVideoInSystem MatroxSystem MediaManager MidiSystem MonitoringManager MovieWriter MtcSystem NewTekNDIRelaySystem NotchLCSubsystem OptiCalCaptureSystem OpticalCalibratorSystem PlaceholderVideoInSystem ProofOfPlaySubsystem ProxyMakerSystem RSCompressedVideoInSystem RecordingSystem RenderStreamSystem ResourceLinks RgbEasySystem SessionDiscoverySystem SessionSystem ShadowResourceHTTPSystem SharedVideoInVideoInSystem SockPuppetSystem SoftEdgeUpdateSystem StreamingACNSystem VideoInCaptureSystem VideoInSystem VideoStitcher WebDownloadManager HelpSystem GuiResourceManager. Domain subclasses (for `domain:`, presumably minus the suffix): MappedMediaDomain MediaInfoDomain MissingMediaDomain NetworkBandwidthDomain NetworkConflictDomain UnusedMediaDomain. Only MonitoringManager, RenderStreamSystem and MappedMedia are doc-verified.

## (d) Python 2.7 caveats for propertyPath
- Version: "Designer uses Python 2.7 for its embedded interpreter ... Use Python 2.7 syntax and standard library features; Be aware of differences from Python 3 (e.g., print is a statement, not a function); String handling, division behavior, and dictionary methods differ from Python 3" https://developer.disguise.one/python-api/environment ; "This needs to be valid Python 2.7 code" https://developer.disguise.one/python-api/execution-api ; LiveUpdate: "Property paths are evaluated as Python expressions in an eval context. The variable object is bound to the resolved subscription object, and all Designer types are available (via from d3 import *)".
- Doc inconsistency to flag: guides/expressions shows f-strings in its Python examples (`seq.setExpression(f"module:{emitter_layer.name}.brightness")`, "Using an f-string is a clean way to build the expression") which contradicts the 2.7 statement on three other pages. Do not rely on f-strings.
- Concrete rules for propertyPath:
  1. `eval` = single expression. No statements: no assignment, `print`, `import`, `for`/`if` blocks, `def`, `lambda` bodies with statements. `:=` does not exist in 2.7.
  2. No f-strings (SyntaxError in 2.7). Use `"%s" % x` or `"{}".format(x)` (`.format` shown on the environment page).
  3. `/` on two ints floors in 2.7. Use `float(a)/b` or `1.0*a/b` for rates/percentages.
  4. Conditional expression `a if cond else b` (2.5+) is the None-guard for the property part, e.g. `object.timecode.statusString if object.timecode else ""`.
  5. List/dict/set comprehensions and generator expressions are all valid in 2.7 (dict comprehensions are used in the LiveUpdate doc). `next(...)`, `sorted`, `min`, `max`, `len`, `range`, `getattr(obj, "name", default)`, `hasattr` (useful-strings uses hasattr) all exist.
  6. `object` shadows the Python builtin `object` inside the eval namespace; do not use `isinstance(x, object)`.
  7. `sys` and `threading` are removed (environment page). `math` is not imported by `from d3 import *`; availability inside the LiveUpdate eval namespace is unverified.
  8. Unicode: 2.7 has separate `str`/`unicode`; string values serialise fine to JSON; string comparisons with literals work. Avoid non-ASCII literals in the path.
  9. Long ints and `0x...` literals are fine (UIDs).
  10. Values produced by comprehensions/method calls are read-only for `set` ("will return all video layers on the named track, but will not allow the client to change any of those layers" - LiveUpdate). Only direct attribute chains ending in a settable property/field (`.v`, `.offset`, `.brightness`) accept `set`.

## Open questions for the lead
1. Case sensitivity of the type prefix (`Machine:` vs `machine:`) is undocumented; the LiveUpdate doc mixes cases. Recommend lowercase and test once on a real Director.
2. Whether the sanitised name is case-folded (a track named "Track 1": `track:track_1` or `track:Track_1`?) and whether the quoted form matches `description` case-sensitively. Recommend quoted form and testing.
3. Whether the default TransportManager is literally named "default" in every project (help example `transportmanager:default` is the only evidence). A fallback is `subsystem:GuiSystem` / `object.currentTransportManager` (d3.pyi:19245), reachability of `subsystem:GuiSystem` unverified.
4. `subsystem:` reachability is only shown for MonitoringManager and RenderStreamSystem; `domain:` only for MappedMedia. The suffix-stripping rule for `domain:` is inferred from one example.
5. `expressionvariablesdevice:` prefix is derived from the lowercase-class rule, never shown in a doc. Also unverified whether `set` on `container.variables[i].defaultFloat` propagates to running expressions without a save.
6. `track:x.getLeafLayers()` with no argument: the pyi only declares `SuperTrack.getLeafLayers(self, type)` (d3.pyi:48147); the doc example calls it with no args.
7. `math` (and other stdlib modules) availability in the LiveUpdate eval namespace is unverified; only `from d3 import *` is documented.
8. Sections have no name property in `SectionInfo` (only iSection/tStart/tEnd/transition); operator-facing section names would have to come from `track.cues`/`track.tags` (types only glimpsed, not verified here).
9. guides/expressions shows f-strings in Python examples, contradicting the Python 2.7 statement on environment/execution-api/introduction pages. Treat 2.7 as authoritative.
10. `TrackPlayer.speed` (r34.0) is getter-only in the changelog; transport speed changes must go through `TransportCommand.makeSetSpeed` + `addCommand`, which LiveUpdate `set` cannot do.
